intent.raw_query: Eastern Europe city hop Prague + Budapest, $1200, 8 days, September 2026

experiences.name: Prague Castle Complex Exploration
experiences.description: Spend a half-day exploring the largest ancient castle complex in the world, including St. Vitus Cathedral, the Old Royal Palace, and Golden Lane. Wander through centuries of Bohemian history with stunning panoramic views over Prague's red rooftops.

experiences.name: Budapest Thermal Bath Experience at Széchenyi
experiences.description: Soak in one of Europe's largest and most iconic thermal bath complexes, built in 1913 in stunning Neo-Baroque style. A deeply cultural Hungarian tradition that blends relaxation, history, and architecture in one unforgettable experience.

experiences.name: Old Town Prague & Astronomical Clock Walking Tour
experiences.description: Explore the medieval Old Town Square, witness the famous 15th-century Astronomical Clock chime on the hour, and stroll through Gothic and Baroque architecture. Join a guided walking tour to uncover the legends and history behind every cobblestone.

experiences.name: Danube River Evening Cruise
experiences.description: Glide along the Danube at sunset and after dark to witness Budapest's illuminated skyline, including the Hungarian Parliament Building, Buda Castle, and Chain Bridge. A breathtaking way to appreciate the city's architectural grandeur from the water.

experiences.name: Budapest Ruin Bar Crawl & Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Discover Budapest's legendary ruin bars born from abandoned Jewish Quarter buildings, while sampling Hungarian street food like lángos (deep-fried dough) and kürtőskalács (chimney cake). A vibrant blend of local culture, nightlife history, and authentic flavors.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Eastern Europe (Prague + Budapest)
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00. Use morning for in-flight rest and preparation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Prague Airport at 13:00. Take Airport Express Bus (Line AE) to Masarykovo nádraží for ~60 CZK (~€2.50), then connect via tram or metro to Hradčany district. Check in to Prague Boutique Stay. Once settled, take a leisurely walk along Nerudova Street, the charming cobblestone lane leading up to Prague Castle — admire the baroque facades and get your bearings in the neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll across Charles Bridge at golden hour for stunning views of the Vltava River and Prague skyline. Explore Malá Strana (Lesser Town) just below the castle — browse the atmospheric side streets and soak in the medieval ambiance of your first evening in Prague.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or grab a snack at the airport upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Pick up a fresh trdelník (chimney cake) or a sausage from a street food stall near Charles Bridge for ~50–80 CZK (~€2–3) to fuel your first afternoon walk.
meals.dinner: Lokál Malá Strana (Míšeňská 12) — a beloved Czech pub serving classic svíčková (beef sirloin with cream sauce) or goulash with bread dumplings for ~180–250 CZK (~€7–10). Pair with a Pilsner Urquell draft.

day_by_day.notes: Buy a 24-hour Prague Public Transport pass (~120 CZK / ~€5) at the airport to cover all tram, metro, and bus rides for the rest of the day and tomorrow morning. Validate your ticket before boarding. September weather in Prague is typically mild (15–20°C), so bring a light jacket for evenings.

day_by_day.morning: Start early with Prague Castle Complex (Pražský hrad) — one of the world's largest castle complexes and just a short walk from your hotel in Hradčany. Visit St. Vitus Cathedral (free exterior, ticket for interior ~250 CZK / ~€10), the Old Royal Palace, and the Golden Lane (a row of tiny colorful medieval houses). Budget ~3 hours. The castle grounds offer sweeping panoramic views over all of Prague.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down through Hradčany Square and visit the Strahov Monastery and its famous Baroque Library (entry ~150 CZK / ~€6) — the frescoed ceiling and ancient tomes are breathtaking. Afterward, descend into Malá Strana and cross Charles Bridge again in daylight to reach the Old Town (Staré Město). Visit the Astronomical Clock (Orloj) on Old Town Square and watch the hourly mechanical show — free to watch from outside.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Old Town Square at dusk — the twin-spired Týn Church and surrounding Gothic architecture are beautifully lit at night. Browse the local shops along Celetná Street. End the evening with a beer at a traditional Czech pub in the Old Town.

meals.breakfast: Grab a fresh pastry (rohlík or koláč) and coffee from a local bakery near Hradčany for ~60–80 CZK (~€2.50–3). Try Café Louvre or a neighborhood pekárna (bakery).
meals.lunch: Nase Maso (Dlouhá 39, Old Town) — a beloved butcher-deli hybrid serving excellent open-faced sandwiches and meat dishes for ~150–200 CZK (~€6–8). Very popular with locals.
meals.dinner: Pivnice U Zlatého Tygra (Husova 17) — a legendary no-frills Czech pub famous for its perfectly poured Pilsner Urquell. Order the pork knee or fried cheese with tartar sauce for ~150–220 CZK (~€6–9).

day_by_day.notes: Prague Castle is best visited early to beat the crowds. The basic circuit ticket (~250 CZK) covers the main highlights — skip the expensive full circuit unless you're a deep history enthusiast. Wear comfortable walking shoes as Hradčany's cobblestones can be tough on feet.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Josefov, Prague's historic Jewish Quarter. Walk through the six surviving synagogues and the haunting Old Jewish Cemetery (combined ticket ~500 CZK / ~€20 — the most expensive but deeply moving cultural experience in Prague). The Pinkas Synagogue, with the names of 77,297 Holocaust victims inscribed on its walls, is particularly powerful.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the river to Vinohrady neighborhood via tram — a residential district with beautiful Art Nouveau architecture, local cafés, and a very non-touristy atmosphere. Visit Náměstí Míru square and the neo-Gothic Church of St. Ludmila. Browse the Jiřák Farmers Market (Saturdays only — if not Saturday, explore the area's independent bookshops and vintage stores instead). Walk through Riegrovy Sady park for panoramic views of Prague and a cold beer at the famous beer garden.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Malá Strana for a sunset walk along the riverside embankment (Nábřeží). Visit the quirky John Lennon Wall — a constantly evolving mural covered in Beatles lyrics and peace messages — free and open 24/7. End the evening exploring the lively bar scene around Náměstí Republiky.

meals.breakfast: Café Savoy (Vítězná 5, Malá Strana) — a grand café with stunning Neo-Renaissance interior. Splurge slightly on a proper Czech breakfast with eggs, cold cuts, and coffee for ~200–280 CZK (~€8–11). Worth it once.
meals.lunch: Grab a falafel wrap or kebab from one of the many affordable spots in Žižkov or Vinohrady for ~100–150 CZK (~€4–6). Try Falafel House on Dlouhá for excellent value.
meals.dinner: Kantýna (Politických vězňů 5) — a modern Czech canteen-style restaurant with excellent grilled meats and fresh salads at very reasonable prices (~200–280 CZK / ~€8–11 for a full meal). Very popular with locals.

day_by_day.notes: The Jewish Quarter ticket is pricey but represents one of the best-preserved Jewish heritage sites in Europe — highly recommended for history lovers. Keep your public transport pass topped up; a 3-day pass (~310 CZK / ~€12.50) is excellent value if you plan to use trams and metro frequently.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip or morning exploration of Vyšehrad — Prague's lesser-known but equally impressive fortress on a cliff above the Vltava River. Free entry to the grounds. Visit the Vyšehrad Cemetery (burial place of Dvořák, Smetana, and other Czech luminaries), the Romanesque rotunda of St. Martin, and walk the ancient ramparts for incredible city views. Far fewer tourists than Prague Castle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Museum (Národní muzeum) on Wenceslas Square — recently renovated and stunning inside (~200 CZK / ~€8 entry). Explore the natural history and Czech history collections. Afterward, walk the length of Wenceslas Square (Václavské náměstí), a grand boulevard central to Czech history — site of the 1989 Velvet Revolution. Visit the St. Wenceslas statue and the memorial to Jan Palach.
day_by_day.evening: Prepare for tomorrow's travel to Budapest. Pack your bags and do a final evening walk through Malá Strana to say goodbye to Prague. Enjoy a farewell Czech beer and dinner near the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Pick up fresh bread, cheese, and fruit from a local Albert supermarket or potraviny (corner store) near Hradčany for a self-catered budget breakfast — ~80–100 CZK (~€3–4).
meals.lunch: Dish (Mánesova 13, Vinohrady) — a casual spot with excellent daily lunch specials (polední menu) including soup + main for ~150–180 CZK (~€6–7). Many Czech restaurants offer great value lunch menus on weekdays.
meals.dinner: U Fleků (Křemencova 11) — Prague's oldest operating brewery (since 1499). A tourist institution but genuinely excellent dark lager brewed on-site. Order the pork roast or goulash for ~200–280 CZK (~€8–11). Lively, atmospheric, and memorable.

day_by_day.notes: Book your Prague to Budapest transport tonight if not already done. The most budget-friendly option is the RegioJet overnight bus or train (~€15–30 one way, ~7–8 hours). Alternatively, FlixBus offers competitive prices. Booking in advance saves significantly. Departure is typically from Praha Florenc bus station or Praha hlavní nádraží (main train station).

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Depart Prague early morning by bus or train to Budapest. The journey takes approximately 6–8 hours by bus (RegioJet/FlixBus) or 6.5 hours by train. Enjoy the scenic Central European countryside — rolling hills, small towns, and river valleys — as you pass through the Czech and Slovak countryside. Arrive at Budapest Keleti or Népliget bus station in the early-to-mid afternoon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to your Budapest accommodation (budget hostel or guesthouse recommended — Retox Party Hostel, Wombats City Hostel, or Carpe Noctem Vitae all offer great value at ~€15–25/night in the city center). Drop your bags and head immediately to the iconic Hungarian Parliament Building (Országház) for exterior photos from the Danube bank — one of the most spectacular Gothic Revival buildings in the world. The riverside promenade (Kossuth Lajos tér) offers stunning views.
day_by_day.evening: Walk across the Chain Bridge (Széchenyi Lánchíd) to Buda side and take the funicular (Budavári Sikló, ~1,200 HUF / ~€3 one way) up to Buda Castle for sweeping panoramic views over the Danube and Pest at sunset. Explore the Fisherman's Bastion (Halászbástya) — free entry in the evening — for fairytale neo-Romanesque turrets and the best night views in Budapest.

meals.breakfast: Pack snacks for the bus/train journey — grab items from a Prague supermarket the night before (bread, cheese, fruit, water) to save money during the travel day.
meals.lunch: On the bus/train — bring your own packed lunch or purchase from a service stop. Budget ~500 HUF (~€1.30) for snacks if buying en route.
meals.dinner: Első Pesti Rétesház (Október 6. utca 22) — Budapest's famous strudel house near St. Stephen's Basilica. Have a light dinner of savory and sweet rétes (strudel) filled with cabbage, cheese, or cherry for ~1,500–2,500 HUF (~€4–7). Quintessentially Hungarian and extremely affordable.

day_by_day.notes: Budapest uses Hungarian Forints (HUF). As of 2027, budget approximately 370–400 HUF per €1 (verify current rates). Budapest is generally cheaper than Prague for food and activities. Buy a 24-hour Budapest public transport pass (~1,650 HUF / ~€4.50) upon arrival — covers all metro, tram, and bus lines. Validate before boarding every time.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Buda Castle (Budavári Palota) and the Castle District in the morning — explore the cobblestone streets of the UNESCO-listed Castle Hill. Visit Matthias Church (Mátyás-templom, entry ~2,500 HUF / ~€6.50) with its stunning Zsolnay tile roof and ornate interior. Walk along the Castle District's medieval streets and admire the mix of Gothic, Baroque, and Art Nouveau architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross back to Pest and visit the Great Market Hall (Nagycsarnok) — Budapest's largest and most beautiful covered market. Browse stalls selling paprika, sausages, embroidered tablecloths, and Hungarian folk crafts on the ground floor. The upper floor has affordable lángos (deep-fried flatbread) stands — a must-try Hungarian street food. Afterward, walk along Váci utca (the main pedestrian shopping street) toward the city center.
day_by_day.evening: Visit St. Stephen's Basilica (Szent István-bazilika) — free entry to the main nave, small fee for the dome (~500 HUF / ~€1.30). The evening organ concerts held here are magical if timed right. Afterward, explore the vibrant ruin bar scene in the Jewish Quarter (District VII) — start at Szimpla Kert, Budapest's most famous ruin bar, set in a crumbling former factory. Entry is free; drinks are cheap by Western standards.

meals.breakfast: Pick up fresh pastries (kifli, pogácsa) from a local pékség (bakery) near your accommodation for ~300–500 HUF (~€0.80–1.30). Pair with a strong espresso from a neighborhood café.
meals.lunch: Lángos from the Great Market Hall upper floor — a classic Hungarian street food of fried dough topped with sour cream and cheese for ~800–1,200 HUF (~€2–3). Incredibly filling and delicious.
meals.dinner: Frici Papa Kifőzdéje (Király utca 55, District VII) — a legendary no-frills Hungarian canteen beloved by locals. Hearty goulash soup, stuffed peppers, and chicken paprikash for ~1,500–2,500 HUF (~€4–6.50). Cash only, arrive early as it fills up fast.

day_by_day.notes: Sunday morning is a great time to visit the Castle District before crowds arrive. The Great Market Hall is open Sunday but closes earlier than weekdays (typically until 3pm on Sundays). The ruin bar scene in District VII (Kazinczy utca area) is best explored on foot — bars are clustered within a few blocks of each other.

day_by_day.morning: Spend the morning at one of Budapest's legendary thermal baths — a quintessential Hungarian experience. The Széchenyi Thermal Bath (Széchenyi gyógyfürdő) is the most iconic, with its grand yellow Neo-Baroque building in City Park (~6,500 HUF / ~€17 for a day ticket with locker). Alternatively, Rudas Baths on the Buda side is more authentic and slightly cheaper (~4,500 HUF / ~€12). Soak in the mineral-rich hot springs and enjoy the surreal experience of bathing in a 100-year-old palace.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the baths, visit Heroes' Square (Hősök tere) — Budapest's grandest public square with the Millennium Monument, featuring statues of the Seven Chieftains of the Magyars and Hungarian kings. Free to visit. Walk through City Park (Városliget) — Budapest's main public park — and see Vajdahunyad Castle (a fairy-tale castle replica built for the 1896 Millennium Exhibition, free exterior). Rent a rowboat on the park lake for ~2,000 HUF (~€5) for a relaxing afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Take a Danube River cruise at sunset — several companies offer 1-hour sightseeing cruises for ~5,000–7,000 HUF (~€13–18). Seeing the illuminated Parliament, Chain Bridge, and Buda Castle from the water at night is one of the most spectacular sights in all of Europe. Book in advance online for the best prices. Afterward, explore the Great Synagogue (Dohány Street Synagogue) area at night — the largest synagogue in Europe, beautifully lit at night (free exterior viewing).

meals.breakfast: Café Gerbeaud (Vörösmarty tér 7) — Budapest's most historic café, established in 1858. Splurge on a coffee and slice of Dobos torte (layered caramel cake) for ~2,500–3,500 HUF (~€6.50–9). An iconic Budapest experience worth the slight splurge.
meals.lunch: Bors GasztroBar (Kazinczy utca 10, District VII) — a tiny, legendary spot serving creative gourmet soups and baguettes for ~1,200–2,000 HUF (~€3–5). Expect a short queue — it moves fast and is absolutely worth it.
meals.dinner: Menza (Liszt Ferenc tér 2) — a stylish but affordable retro-communist-themed restaurant serving elevated Hungarian classics. Main courses ~3,500–5,000 HUF (~€9–13). Excellent value for a slightly more upscale dinner on your penultimate evening.

day_by_day.notes: Bring a towel and flip-flops to the thermal baths (or rent towels on-site for ~500 HUF). The Széchenyi Baths are best on weekday mornings before tour groups arrive. Book the Danube cruise online in advance — Legenda and Mahart PassNave are reputable operators. The cruise typically includes commentary about the illuminated landmarks.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Budapest — visit the Hungarian National Museum (Magyar Nemzeti Múzeum, entry ~2,200 HUF / ~€6) for a comprehensive overview of Hungarian history from prehistoric times through the 20th century, including the Hungarian Crown Jewels. Beautifully presented in a grand Neo-Classical building. Alternatively, visit the Dohány Street Synagogue and its adjacent Holocaust Memorial (the Tree of Life sculpture) for ~4,500 HUF (~€12) — deeply moving and historically significant.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final stroll along the Danube Promenade (Duna-korzó) on the Pest side for last views of the Buda hills and Chain Bridge. Browse the riverside souvenir stalls for affordable paprika, pálinka (fruit brandy), and folk art gifts. Head to your departure point — Budapest Keleti railway station or Liszt Ferenc International Airport depending on your onward travel. Budapest Airport is accessible via Bus 100E (~900 HUF / ~€2.50, direct to the city center).
day_by_day.evening: Departure or final evening in Budapest. If departing late, enjoy a farewell dinner in the Jewish Quarter before heading to the airport or station.

meals.breakfast: New York Café (Erzsébet körút 9-11) — the most beautiful café in the world, housed in a jaw-dropping gilded palace. Coffee and pastry runs ~2,500–4,000 HUF (~€6.50–10). A spectacular way to end your trip — arrive right when it opens (9am) to beat the crowds.
meals.lunch: Hummus Bar (Alkotmány utca 20 or multiple locations) — a Budapest institution serving enormous portions of hummus with pita and toppings for ~1,500–2,500 HUF (~€4–6.50). Great for a quick, filling, budget-friendly final lunch.
meals.dinner: If staying for an evening departure: Fülemüle (Kisdiófa utca 7) — a hidden gem in District VII serving traditional Hungarian home cooking in a cozy setting. Chicken paprikash with nokedli dumplings or stuffed cabbage for ~2,500–3,500 HUF (~€6.50–9). A perfect farewell to Hungarian cuisine.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 90 minutes to reach Budapest Airport from the city center during peak hours. The 100E airport bus runs every 20 minutes and is by far the cheapest option (~€2.50 vs. ~€30–40 for a taxi). Keep some HUF for the bus fare. Total estimated budget for the full 8-day trip (excluding flights): €300–420 per person, covering accommodation (~€10–20/night in Budapest), food (~€20–30/day), transport, and entry fees. Prague is slightly more expensive than Budapest but both cities offer exceptional value for budget travelers.

trip_options.title: Classic Eastern Europe (Prague + Budapest) Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Prague Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer to Hradčany district boutique hotel via airport express bus to Dejvická metro station, then short taxi/tram ride. Check in, freshen up, and get oriented.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely walk around the Hradčany neighborhood to shake off travel fatigue. Stroll along Loretánská Street to the Loreta Shrine (a stunning Baroque pilgrimage site), then walk to the Hradčany Square (Hradčanské náměstí) to admire the Archbishop's Palace and get your first views of Prague Castle's exterior. Keep the pace relaxed — this is an orientation afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Head down the castle hill to Malá Strana (Lesser Town) via the Old Castle Steps. Explore the charming cobblestone streets and cross the iconic Charles Bridge at dusk for atmospheric views of the Vltava River and illuminated castle behind you. Enjoy a relaxed first dinner in Malá Strana.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and pastry at the airport or on arrival — nothing formal scheduled before check-in.
meals.lunch: Light snack or sandwich from a local bakery near the hotel after settling in (e.g., Pekárna Nostress or a nearby café in Hradčany).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Café Savoy in Malá Strana — a beautifully restored Neo-Renaissance café serving Czech classics like svíčková (beef sirloin in cream sauce) and roast duck. Mid-range pricing, excellent atmosphere. Budget ~600–900 CZK per person.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light. Focus on getting settled and absorbing the neighborhood atmosphere rather than rushing to tick off sights. September in Prague is mild (15–20°C), ideal for evening walks. Wear comfortable walking shoes from day one — Hradčany's cobblestones are uneven.

day_by_day.morning: Full Prague Castle Complex visit — start early to beat crowds. Explore St. Vitus Cathedral (marvel at the stained glass and Gothic architecture), the Old Royal Palace (Vladislav Hall), St. George's Basilica, and the Golden Lane (Zlatá ulička), a row of tiny colorful historic houses where Franz Kafka once lived. Purchase a combined ticket (~350 CZK) for access to all areas.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down through the castle gardens (Rampart Garden or South Gardens) with panoramic city views. Head into Malá Strana and visit the Church of St. Nicholas, one of the finest Baroque churches in Central Europe. Explore the Malá Strana neighborhood at your own pace — peek into hidden courtyards and browse local shops.
day_by_day.evening: Cross Charles Bridge again (now you know it well) into the Old Town (Staré Město). Visit the Old Town Square to see the Astronomical Clock (Orloj) perform its hourly show, and admire the Church of Our Lady before Týn. Wander the Old Town's medieval lanes.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or nearby — try Eska Bakery (a short tram ride away) for excellent Czech sourdough bread, pastries, and specialty coffee. Budget ~150–250 CZK.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Lokál Hradčany or a nearby pivnice (traditional Czech pub) — try goulash with bread dumplings and a half-liter of Pilsner Urquell. Budget ~250–400 CZK.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Kolkovna Celnice in Old Town — a popular Czech restaurant with great atmosphere, serving traditional dishes like pork knee, roast duck, and fresh-tapped beer. Budget ~500–800 CZK per person.

day_by_day.notes: Prague Castle is one of the largest castle complexes in the world — wear comfortable shoes and plan for 3–4 hours minimum. Book cathedral tower access in advance if you want the climb. The Astronomical Clock performs at the top of every hour; the 6 PM show draws large crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Jewish Quarter (Josefov) — one of the best-preserved Jewish quarters in Europe. Visit the Old Jewish Cemetery (one of the most haunting and historically significant sites in Prague), the Old-New Synagogue (the oldest active synagogue in Europe, built in 1270), and the Pinkas Synagogue with its memorial to Holocaust victims. Combined ticket ~500 CZK.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along the Royal Route from Old Town toward Wenceslas Square (Václavské náměstí) in the New Town. Visit the National Museum at the top of the square (recently renovated, excellent Czech history exhibits). Explore the Art Nouveau Municipal House (Obecní dům) — free to walk through the lobby; guided tours available.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a classical music concert — Prague has numerous affordable evening concerts in historic churches and venues. Options include concerts at St. George's Basilica, the Municipal House, or the Klementinum Mirror Chapel. Tickets typically ~400–700 CZK. Afterwards, explore the vibrant Vinohrady neighborhood for a nightcap.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or Grand Café Orient in Old Town — a reconstructed Cubist café (a uniquely Czech architectural style) serving coffee, pastries, and light bites. Budget ~150–200 CZK.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Naše Maso — a beloved Prague butcher-restaurant in Old Town serving excellent open-faced sandwiches (chlebíčky), tartare, and quality Czech meats. Budget ~200–350 CZK.
meals.dinner: Pre-concert dinner at Café Imperial — an Art Nouveau gem with stunning mosaic tile walls, serving elevated Czech and European cuisine. Budget ~600–900 CZK per person.

day_by_day.notes: Josefov is emotionally heavy — allow time to process the history. The Jewish Quarter museums are closed on Saturdays (Shabbat), so Thursday is ideal. Book concert tickets in advance online — September is peak cultural season in Prague.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip or morning exploration of Vyšehrad — Prague's second castle and a less-visited gem. Walk the fortified walls for sweeping Vltava views, visit the Romanesque Rotunda of St. Martin (Prague's oldest standing building), and explore the Vyšehrad Cemetery where Czech luminaries like Dvořák and Mucha are buried. Peaceful and crowd-free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the city center and visit the Mucha Museum (dedicated to Art Nouveau master Alfons Mucha) or the Prague City Museum for deeper Czech history context. Alternatively, explore the Letná Park area and visit the National Technical Museum if you enjoy industrial history. End the afternoon with a walk across Nusle Bridge for dramatic views.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Prague — explore the Žižkov neighborhood, known for its bohemian character and quirky Žižkov Television Tower (you can spot the crawling baby sculptures from afar and take the elevator up for city views, ~180 CZK). Enjoy Prague's nightlife scene with a craft beer at one of Žižkov's many local pubs.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel — fuel up before the Vyšehrad walk.
meals.lunch: Lunch near Vyšehrad at Restaurace Vyšehrad or a picnic in the park with supplies from a local deli — September weather is perfect for outdoor eating. Budget ~200–350 CZK.
meals.dinner: Farewell Prague dinner at Mincovna on Old Town Square — solid Czech cuisine in a historic setting with good value for location. Try the roasted pork with sauerkraut and potato dumplings. Budget ~500–750 CZK per person.

day_by_day.notes: Pack your bags tonight — tomorrow morning you travel to Budapest. Vyšehrad is easily reached by metro (Line C, Vyšehrad station). The Television Tower is best visited at sunset for the best light and views.

day_by_day.morning: Morning train from Prague to Budapest — the RegioJet or Czech Railways/MÁV train departs Prague Main Station (Praha Hlavní Nádraží) and arrives at Budapest-Keleti Station in approximately 6.5–7 hours. Book tickets in advance (~€25–50 per person). The journey passes through beautiful Bohemian and Slovak countryside. Enjoy the scenic ride with snacks and coffee from the dining car.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive Budapest Keleti around 14:00–15:00. Check in to your mid-range accommodation (recommended: Pest side near the Jewish Quarter or Andrássy Avenue for central access). Freshen up, then take a first walk to Heroes' Square (Hősök tere) and the edge of City Park (Városliget) to get your bearings in Budapest.
day_by_day.evening: Walk down the elegant Andrássy Avenue (a UNESCO World Heritage boulevard) toward the State Opera House. Admire the Neo-Renaissance architecture. End at the lively Great Market Hall area or the ruin bars district in the Jewish Quarter (VII District) for a first taste of Budapest's unique nightlife scene.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel or grab supplies at Prague Main Station before boarding — pastries, sandwiches, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch on the train from the dining car or packed snacks. Budget ~€8–15.
meals.dinner: First Budapest dinner at Borkonyha Winekitchen near the Basilica — a Michelin Bib Gourmand restaurant offering modern Hungarian cuisine at mid-range prices. Try the foie gras, beef cheek, or seasonal Hungarian dishes paired with local wines. Budget ~8,000–12,000 HUF per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Prague–Budapest train is one of Europe's great scenic rail journeys — sit on the right side heading south for the best views. Book train tickets at least 2–3 weeks ahead for best prices and seat reservations. September weekends fill up quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Cross the Danube to Buda for a full Buda Castle Hill day. Take the historic Funicular (Budavári Sikló, ~1,200 HUF) up from Chain Bridge. Explore Buda Castle and the Hungarian National Gallery (housed inside the castle, free on Sundays for EU citizens, otherwise ~3,200 HUF) — excellent collection of Hungarian fine art. Walk to Matthias Church and the Fisherman's Bastion for iconic panoramic views over Pest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend the castle hill and walk across the iconic Chain Bridge (Széchenyi Lánchíd) — one of Budapest's most recognizable landmarks. Visit the Hungarian Parliament Building exterior from the Pest bank — it's one of the world's most beautiful parliamentary buildings. Book a guided interior tour in advance (~6,000 HUF) if interested.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Great Synagogue on Dohány Street — the largest synagogue in Europe and a moving memorial to Budapest's Jewish history (tours run until late afternoon; check closing times). Then head into the ruin bar district: visit Szimpla Kert, the original and most famous ruin bar, for drinks in a wonderfully eccentric converted building.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or at Gerbeaud Café on Vörösmarty Square — Budapest's most historic café, open since 1858. Try the Gerbeaud cake (layered sponge with apricot jam and chocolate). Budget ~2,500–4,000 HUF.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Ruszwurm Cukrászda, a tiny historic pastry shop on Castle Hill (open since 1827) — grab a slice of Dobos torte and coffee. For a full meal, try Pest-Buda Bistro nearby for Hungarian classics. Budget ~3,000–5,000 HUF.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Mazel Tov in the Jewish Quarter — a beautifully designed Middle Eastern-Hungarian fusion restaurant in a stunning greenhouse-style ruin space. Excellent mezze platters and grilled dishes. Budget ~6,000–9,000 HUF per person.

day_by_day.notes: Sunday in Budapest is ideal for Buda Castle — slightly fewer crowds than weekdays. The Hungarian National Gallery is free for EU citizens on Sundays. Fisherman's Bastion is free to walk around (small fee for tower access). Ruin bars are busiest on weekends — arrive at Szimpla Kert by 20:00 for a good spot.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day at the famous Széchenyi Thermal Baths in City Park — one of Budapest's must-do experiences. The grand Neo-Baroque bath complex has indoor and outdoor thermal pools, steam rooms, and saunas. September is perfect for the outdoor pools as the air cools but the water stays warm (~38°C). Arrive early (9:00) to avoid crowds. Budget ~7,000–9,000 HUF for entry.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through City Park (Városliget) and visit the Vajdahunyad Castle (a fairy-tale complex built for the 1896 Millennium Exhibition, free to enter grounds). Visit the Museum of Fine Arts adjacent to Heroes' Square (excellent European art collection, ~3,200 HUF). Walk back down Andrássy Avenue, stopping to admire the architecture and boutique shops.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the House of Terror Museum on Andrássy Avenue — a powerful and sobering museum documenting Hungary's Nazi and Soviet occupation periods, housed in the former secret police headquarters. (Check closing times — typically closes by 18:00.) Afterwards, enjoy a sunset cruise on the Danube to see Budapest's illuminated bridges and Parliament from the water (~5,000–8,000 HUF for 1-hour cruise).

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before the baths — grab a coffee and pastry at a nearby café, or eat at the hotel. Keep it light before swimming.
meals.lunch: Lunch inside Széchenyi Baths restaurant or at a nearby eatery in City Park. Alternatively, try Bagolyvár Restaurant next to the zoo — a charming Hungarian restaurant. Budget ~3,500–5,500 HUF.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Costes Downtown on the Pest riverbank — a Michelin-starred restaurant with an accessible tasting menu option. A splurge-worthy experience for a special evening. Budget ~15,000–22,000 HUF per person. (Or for mid-range: Belvárosi Lugas nearby, excellent Hungarian cuisine at ~5,000–8,000 HUF.)

day_by_day.notes: Book Széchenyi Baths online in advance — Monday mornings are among the quieter times. Bring flip-flops, a towel, and a swimsuit. The House of Terror is emotionally intense — allow 1.5–2 hours. The Danube evening cruise is highly recommended for a different perspective of the city's stunning architecture.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Budapest — visit the Central Market Hall (Nagy Vásárcsarnok) for a vibrant sensory experience of Hungarian food culture. Browse stalls selling paprika, salami, Tokaji wine, embroidered textiles, and Hungarian souvenirs. Pick up gifts and taste local delicacies like lángos (deep-fried dough with sour cream and cheese) from a market stall.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time: Visit the Hungarian National Museum for a comprehensive overview of Hungarian history from prehistoric times to the present (~1,600 HUF). Alternatively, take a final walk along the Danube Promenade on the Pest side, cross to Buda via the Elizabeth Bridge for one last view, and visit the Cave Church (Sziklatemplom) built into the cliffs of Gellért Hill. Climb Gellért Hill to the Citadella for a final panoramic farewell view of Budapest.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport or Budapest-Keleti Station depending on onward travel plans. Allow 45–60 minutes for airport transfer by metro + shuttle or taxi (~6,000–8,000 HUF by taxi).

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel — final proper sit-down meal before checkout.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Gundel Restaurant near City Park (Budapest's most historic grand restaurant, open since 1894) for a celebratory final lunch — try the Gundel pancakes (flambéed crêpes with walnut filling and chocolate sauce). Budget ~8,000–14,000 HUF per person. Or lighter option: a bowl of gulyás soup at a local étterem near the market. Budget ~2,500–4,000 HUF.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the airport or en route, depending on departure time — grab a final Hungarian pastry (rétes/strudel) and espresso before leaving.

day_by_day.notes: The Central Market Hall closes early on Sundays and Mondays — Tuesday is ideal. Pack paprika and salami carefully in checked luggage (EU regulations allow food products between EU countries). Allow extra time for airport security in September — peak travel season. Keep some HUF for last-minute purchases; exchange or use ATM at the market.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Eastern Europe (Prague + Budapest) Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Prague Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private airport transfer arranged via luxury chauffeur service to Boutique Stay in Hradčany district. Check-in, freshen up, and settle into your suite.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation walk through the Hradčany Castle Quarter. Stroll along Hradčanské náměstí (Hradčany Square), admire the Archbishop's Palace and Schwarzenberg Palace exteriors, and take in the sweeping panoramic views over Prague's red-roofed skyline from the castle ramparts. Visit the St. Vitus Cathedral interior for a first taste of Gothic grandeur.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset walk across the iconic Charles Bridge, watching the city glow in golden hour light. Explore the atmospheric Malá Strana (Lesser Town) cobblestone lanes. Dinner at a premium restaurant in the neighbourhood.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or at airport)
meals.lunch: Light welcome lunch at the hotel or a nearby artisan café in Hradčany upon arrival — try Café Savoy (Vítězná 5) for elegant Czech pastries and open-faced sandwiches
meals.dinner: Augustine Restaurant at The Augustine Hotel, Malá Strana — refined Czech-European cuisine in a converted 13th-century Augustinian monastery; try the slow-roasted duck with red cabbage and bread dumplings paired with a Moravian wine

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the 13:00 arrival. Request early check-in in advance. Hradčany is walkable to all afternoon and evening spots — no transport needed. September in Prague is mild (15–20°C), ideal for evening strolls.

day_by_day.morning: Full Prague Castle Complex private guided tour (3 hours). Explore St. Vitus Cathedral in depth, the Old Royal Palace with its Vladislav Hall, the Basilica of St. George, and the charming Golden Lane (Zlatá ulička) — the row of tiny medieval artisan houses. A private expert guide adds historical context unavailable to general visitors.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend into Malá Strana for a curated visit to the Baroque Wallenstein Palace and its stunning formal gardens — a hidden gem largely overlooked by tourists. Continue to the Kafka Museum on the riverbank for a thought-provoking cultural detour into Prague's literary soul. Optionally visit the Lobkowicz Palace inside the castle complex for its private art collection (Canaletto, Velázquez) and classical music concert.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a private chamber music concert — the Lobkowicz Palace concerts or a Mozart/Dvořák evening at the Liechtenstein Palace are world-class options in intimate Baroque settings. Dinner in Malá Strana afterward.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast at your Hradčany boutique property — request a full Czech spread with cold cuts, Olomouc cheese, fresh rye bread, and strong Arabica coffee
meals.lunch: Terasa U Zlaté Studně (At the Golden Well) — a Michelin-recommended rooftop restaurant perched above Malá Strana with extraordinary castle views; try the Czech beef tenderloin with truffle sauce
meals.dinner: Kampa Park — Prague's legendary fine-dining riverside institution on Kampa Island; celebrated for its duck confit, river views, and extensive wine cellar

day_by_day.notes: Book the Lobkowicz Palace concert and private castle guide well in advance — these sell out weeks ahead. The Golden Lane is included in the main castle ticket. Wear comfortable shoes for cobblestones.

day_by_day.morning: Private walking tour of the Old Town (Staré Město). Begin at the Old Town Square to witness the Astronomical Clock (Orloj) chime at the top of the hour. Explore the Church of Our Lady before Týn, the Baroque St. Nicholas Church, and the medieval Ungelt courtyard. Enter the Jewish Quarter (Josefov) — visit the six historic synagogues and the Old Jewish Cemetery with a private cultural guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Municipal House (Obecní dům) — Prague's finest Art Nouveau masterpiece — for a guided interior tour of its Smetana Hall and ornate salons. Walk the Pařížská Boulevard (Prague's equivalent of the Champs-Élysées) for luxury boutique browsing. Visit the Museum of Decorative Arts for exquisite Bohemian glass, porcelain, and furniture collections.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a performance at the stunning Neo-Rococo Estates Theatre (Stavovské divadlo) — the very hall where Mozart personally premiered Don Giovanni in 1787. Dinner in the Old Town before or after the performance.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: La Degustation Bohême Bourgeoise — one of Prague's two Michelin-starred restaurants; a multi-course tasting menu celebrating historic Bohemian recipes reimagined with modern technique; book well ahead
meals.dinner: Alcron Restaurant (Radisson Blu Alcron Hotel) — intimate Art Deco fine dining with exceptional seafood; Prague's other Michelin star; try the signature lobster bisque

day_by_day.notes: The Jewish Quarter requires a combined ticket covering all synagogues — purchase in advance online to skip queues. Estates Theatre tickets should be booked 4–6 weeks ahead for premium seats. The Old Town is approximately 20 minutes by taxi or Uber from Hradčany.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Kutná Hora (1.5 hours from Prague by private transfer). Visit the extraordinary Sedlec Ossuary (Bone Church) — a medieval chapel decorated with the bones of 40,000 people, one of Europe's most hauntingly unique sites. Continue to the UNESCO-listed Cathedral of St. Barbara, a breathtaking Gothic masterpiece rivalling St. Vitus.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Kutná Hora's beautifully preserved medieval silver-mining town centre — the Italian Court (former royal mint), the Stone House, and the main Palacký Square. Return to Prague by private transfer in the late afternoon, arriving back by 17:00.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening in Prague. Sunset cocktails at the rooftop bar of the Hotel Aria or the Mandarin Oriental terrace in Malá Strana. Leisurely dinner without rushing.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast — early start recommended for Kutná Hora
meals.lunch: Restaurace Dačický in Kutná Hora — a charming historic restaurant in a 16th-century building serving traditional Bohemian game dishes (venison goulash, wild boar) and local Kutná Hora beer
meals.dinner: Eska Restaurant, Prague — a celebrated farm-to-table modern Czech restaurant in the Žižkov district; known for its wood-fired dishes, sourdough bread, and natural wine list; book ahead

day_by_day.notes: Private car transfer to Kutná Hora is strongly recommended over public trains for comfort and flexibility. The Ossuary can be emotionally intense — it is a genuine place of burial and should be treated with respect. Allow 45 minutes at the Ossuary and 2 hours at St. Barbara's Cathedral.

day_by_day.morning: Departure from Prague to Budapest via premium transport. Options: Luxury private car transfer (4.5 hours through picturesque Bohemian and Slovakian countryside) or RegioJet/Leo Express first-class train (6.5 hours with panoramic windows and meal service). Depart by 08:00–09:00 to arrive in Budapest by early-to-mid afternoon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive Budapest and check into your luxury hotel (recommended: Four Seasons Hotel Gresham Palace or Párisi Udvar Hotel Budapest — both iconic landmarks). After settling in, take a private introductory walk along the Danube Promenade (Duna-korzó), admiring the Parliament Building from across the river. Cross the iconic Chain Bridge on foot to Castle Hill.
day_by_day.evening: First evening in Budapest — explore the illuminated Buda Castle District at dusk. The castle, Fisherman's Bastion, and Matthias Church are dramatically lit after dark. Dinner in the Castle District.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast in Prague before departure or on-board dining if travelling by premium train
meals.lunch: On-board or a stop at a scenic Slovak or Hungarian roadside estate restaurant if travelling by private car — ask your driver to suggest a local gem
meals.dinner: Alabárdos Restaurant, Buda Castle District — one of Budapest's most celebrated fine-dining institutions set in a 15th-century Gothic building; Hungarian royal cuisine with dishes like venison in juniper berry sauce and Tokaji Aszú wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Book private transfer or train tickets well in advance, especially for a Saturday departure. The Four Seasons Gresham Palace is on the Pest side directly at the Chain Bridge — ideal location for the rest of the trip. Confirm Budapest hotel check-in time and arrange luggage handling.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of Buda Castle Hill complex. Visit the Hungarian National Gallery (inside the Royal Palace) for masterworks of Hungarian painting and sculpture. Explore the medieval Castle District streets — Úri utca, Tárnok utca — and the Labyrinth of Buda Castle underground. Enjoy the extraordinary Danube panorama from Fisherman's Bastion (Halászbástya) — arguably Europe's finest river view.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the Chain Bridge to Pest. Visit the Hungarian Parliament Building on a private VIP guided tour — one of the world's largest and most beautiful parliament buildings, featuring the Holy Crown of Saint Stephen. Walk along Andrássy Avenue (Budapest's Champs-Élysées, a UNESCO World Heritage street) to Heroes' Square (Hősök tere) and the Millenary Monument. Visit the Museum of Fine Arts for its outstanding collection of Old Masters.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Budapest's legendary thermal spa culture. Book a private evening session at the Széchenyi Thermal Baths or the exclusive Gellért Baths — both are architectural masterpieces. Dinner in the Jewish Quarter (Erzsébetváros).

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — the Four Seasons Gresham Palace breakfast is exceptional with Danube views
meals.lunch: Halászbástya Restaurant at Fisherman's Bastion — elegant terrace dining with unrivalled Parliament and Danube views; try the Hungarian fish soup (halászlé) and grilled fogas (pike-perch from Lake Balaton)
meals.dinner: Onyx Restaurant — Budapest's Michelin two-starred flagship; located on Vörösmarty Square; a theatrical tasting menu celebrating Hungarian ingredients with avant-garde technique; one of Central Europe's finest dining experiences; essential advance booking

day_by_day.notes: Parliament tours must be pre-booked online. The VIP private tour includes access to the Crown Jewels room. Széchenyi Baths are open until 22:00 — the evening atmosphere with lit pools is magical. Bring a swimsuit and towel or rent on-site.

day_by_day.morning: Private Danube river cruise on a chartered luxury vessel (2 hours). See Budapest from the water — the Parliament, Chain Bridge, Buda Castle, Gellért Hill, and Margaret Island from a perspective unavailable on land. Many operators offer private morning cruises with champagne breakfast service.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Great Synagogue on Dohány Street (Dohány utcai zsinagóga) — the largest synagogue in Europe and the second largest in the world; a profoundly moving cultural and historical site with an attached Holocaust memorial garden. Explore the atmospheric Great Market Hall (Nagycsarnok) for Hungarian paprika, Tokaji wine, handcrafted embroidery, and foie gras — ideal for premium gifts and souvenirs. Visit the Hungarian State Opera House for a guided interior tour of its breathtaking Neo-Renaissance auditorium.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a performance at the Hungarian State Opera — one of the world's top opera venues with world-class acoustics and an extraordinary programme. Alternatively, attend a concert at the Liszt Ferenc Academy of Music, Budapest's premier concert hall. Late dinner after the performance.

meals.breakfast: Champagne breakfast on the private Danube cruise
meals.lunch: Gerbeaud Café on Vörösmarty Square — Budapest's most iconic café since 1858; indulge in the legendary Gerbeaud cake (layered sponge with apricot jam and chocolate) and a proper Hungarian coffee; also serves light lunches
meals.dinner: Costes Restaurant — Budapest's first Michelin-starred restaurant; innovative European cuisine with Hungarian seasonal ingredients; intimate setting near the Great Market Hall

day_by_day.notes: Opera tickets should be booked 4–6 weeks in advance for premium seats — check the Hungarian State Opera website directly. The Great Market Hall is closed Sundays but open Monday. The Dohány Street Synagogue requires modest dress (shoulders and knees covered).

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Budapest — visit Gellért Hill (Gellért-hegy) for the most panoramic view of the entire city, the Danube, and both Buda and Pest stretching to the horizon. Walk up through the terraced gardens to the Citadella fortress and the Liberty Statue. A perfect contemplative farewell to the city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisure time for last-minute luxury shopping on Váci utca or Andrássy Avenue (Hermès, Louis Vuitton, and premium Hungarian brands). Alternatively, a final spa session at the Gellért Thermal Baths — a stunning Art Nouveau spa at the foot of Gellért Hill. Farewell lunch at a celebrated Budapest restaurant. Private transfer to Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Budapest. Reflect on 8 extraordinary days across two of Central Europe's most magnificent capitals.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — linger over coffee and pastries with Danube views
meals.lunch: Borkonyha Winekitchen — Michelin-starred Hungarian wine-focused restaurant near the Basilica of St. Stephen; exceptional Hungarian wine list with over 200 labels; try the duck liver with Tokaji Aszú reduction as a final Hungarian farewell
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight — pack a selection of Hungarian salami, paprika, and Tokaji wine purchased at the Great Market Hall as a delicious in-flight memory

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for the airport transfer and check-in from central Budapest (traffic can be heavy). Consider arranging luggage storage at the hotel until your transfer time so you can enjoy the morning freely. Tipping in Hungary is customary at 10–15% in restaurants.
